label: adult-s1
summary: The model (training AUC 0.907) predicts the chance of a low income (the dataset's lower income class) as a sigmoid of an additive score with seven parts, so on the score each part's effect adds to the others. Household status matters most (switching that part off drops the AUC to 0.836): being married to a civilian spouse pulls the prediction well away from a low income, and for the typical married husband the predicted chance of a low income is 72% against 97% for the same man single and living outside a family. Capital gains come next (0.885 without them) and act through two stacked hinges that steepen the effect from gains of about 4000 US dollars: the typical person's predicted chance falls from 72% with no gains to 55% at 3500 US dollars and 1.2% at 10000 US dollars. Education lowers the predicted chance along the education-num scale, with a master's degree getting slightly more than a bachelor's (31% against 30%). Age and weekly hours act as straight lines on the score with no turn-down at older ages; an executive or managerial occupation has its own gate, on for the 4853 executives. Several rare categories carry large fitted offsets that make a low income certain in the model: preschool education (64 rows), never having worked (9 rows), and birth in the Dominican Republic (82) or Guatemala (72). A nine-node branch keyed to birth in Italy is nearly inert (AUC 0.9069 without it, the same as with it), and the seven-node stack inside it changes 0 training predictions when switched off.

tool_bugs: (1) A --calls batch of 6 add_identity_node + 7 split_node calls stopped after the 5th call with nothing on stdout; the 6th identity node and the splits were not applied. Rerunning them in smaller batches worked. (2) The number lint keeps a trailing comma on a token ('$3,500,'), so allow_numbers needed both '$3,500' and '$3,500,'. (3) xn.py --render has no allow_numbers option, so the summary cannot use literal probe inputs such as dollar amounts; worked around by referencing the probe's rows[k].inputs strings. (4) get_formula returns no provenance id, so the formula evidence is a LaTeX payload with its tolerance taken from check_explanation. (5) A leaf cannot use another leaf's exit (3996) as its entry ('already covered'), so the Italy switch and the stack feeding it went into one leaf. (6) query_ablate 'baseline' treats the always-on ReLU 194 as gated and sets it to 0, so the capital_gains ablation also removes 194's mean offset (this is in the AUC loss quoted for that part).

refuted_and_fixed: household: the first draft said men get a lower predicted chance than women; the wife probe gives a married wife a lower chance than a husband, so the claim was restricted to people outside marriage
education: 'the master's edge cancels the extra step' was wrong (the master's degree gets a slightly higher chance than a bachelor's), reworded to 'outweighs'
occupation: 'biggest pull of the occupations' was checked against a probe of all fifteen codes before it was kept
